title: Cheese and Onion Pie
subtitle: A Northern shortcrust pie of sharp cheese and soft onions
excerpt: Soft cooked onions and plenty of mature cheddar in a shortcrust case, baked until the top is deep gold. A cheap, filling supper that slices well hot or cold.
sourceNotes: Northern English baking tradition, adapted for a standard 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead and serve cold, or warm gently before serving.

content.text: This is a plain pie that lives on sharp cheese and slowly cooked onions. Cook the onions until they are soft and sweet, with no raw bite left. Let the filling cool before it goes near the pastry or the base will turn greasy.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Melt the butter in the frying pan over a low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt.
Cook the onions gently for 15 minutes until soft and pale gold. Stir often. Tip them onto a plate and leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a little overhang.
Stir the cheese and mustard through the cooled onions. Season with black pepper. Pile the filling into the case.
Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg, lay the lid on, and press the edges to seal.
Trim the edges and cut a small slit in the top. Brush all over with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep gold. Let it sit for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.cause: The onion filling went in warm, or the cheese was watery.
items.fix: Cool the filling fully and bake on a preheated baking sheet for a crisper base.

items.cause: The edges were not sealed firmly.
items.fix: Press the rim with a fork and chill the assembled pie for 15 minutes before baking.

items.symptom: The top browns before the base sets.
items.fix: Cover the top loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes.
